channel.title: Bloomberg — Reuters/Bloomberg pool
channel.description: Provenance-aware feed; classification fields distinguish exact wire copies from citations.

item.title: Unitree IPO: Why Investors Are Betting Big on China’s Humanoid Robots
item.description: Robots built to move, work and act like humans. It’s a global industry Morgan Stanley estimates could be worth $5 trillion by 2050. It’s also one of the frontiers in the China-US race for technological supremacy.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Pony AI CEO Peng Optimistic on Growth Outlook
item.description: James Peng, CEO of Pony AI, says the company plans to expand its robotaxi fleet across more Chinese cities to meet growing demand. He speaks to David Ingles and Yvonne Man on "Bloomberg: The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LG AI Research's Lee on The Importance of Sovereign AI
item.description: LG AI Research Head of Superintelligence Lab Lee Moon Tae shares his perspective on the future of superintelligence, the opportunities it unlocks and the responsibilities that come with building AI for the next era. He speaks with Haslinda Amin from the sidelines of 'AI Summit Seoul & Expo 2026'. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Alphabet Set to Price Long Aussie Bond With Record Yield Near 7%
item.description: Alphabet Inc. is poised to pay just under 7% to borrow longer-dated funds in its debut Australian dollar bond deal, in potentially its highest-ever coupon, underscoring how broader demands for cash among hyperscalers around the world are feeding into more costly funding almost everywhere.
item.dc:creator: Finbarr Flynn, Matthew Burgess and Sharon Klyne

item.title: Motif Technologies CEO on Business Strategy, AI
item.description: Junghwan Lim, CEO of Korean AI startup Motif Technologies, discusses the company’s business strategy as it works to develop AI models capable of competing with leading global frontier models. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Paul Allen from the AI Summit & Expo in Seoul. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rebellions CFO: Preparing for IPO in Korea
item.description: Sungkyue Shin, CFO of AI chip startup Rebellions, says the company is in active preparations for an IPO, with a listing on South Korea's main stock exchange as its top priority. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Paul Allen from the sidelines of the AI Summit & Expo in Seoul. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Funding $1 Trillion AI Capex May Expand Bond Supply, Robeco Says
item.description: A roughly $1 trillion wave of capital spending tied to artificial intelligence could add to bond supply and keep fixed-income markets volatile as hyperscalers race to fund infrastructure, according to the head of fixed income for Asia at Robeco.
item.dc:creator: Harry Suhartono

item.title: Bain Unit Proterial Seeks $1.3 Billion From Japan Wire Firm Sale
item.description: Bain Capital subsidiary Proterial Ltd. is considering selling its wire, cable and automotive parts businesses, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Takako Taniguchi

item.title: WiseTech Raided by Australia Antitrust Watchdog; Stock Sinks
item.description: WiseTech Global Ltd. said Australian antitrust authorities demanded the company hand over documents and data as part of an investigation into alleged breaches of competition law. The company’s stock tumbled.
item.dc:creator: Angus Whitley

item.title: China Lands Rocket Back on Earth in Push to Catch Up With SpaceX
item.description: China said it recovered a rocket booster on land for the first time, a major step toward catching up with US firms like Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
item.dc:creator: Josh Xiao and Danny Lee

item.title: AI Startup Temporal in Talks for a Valuation of at Least $12 Billion
item.description: Temporal Technologies Inc. is in talks for a fresh funding round that would give the AI startup a valuation of at least $12 billion before the new money, according to people familiar with the efforts.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence, Edward Ludlow and Dina Bass

item.title: Cerebras (CBRS) Says Its New Computer Boosts AI Speed Advantage Over Nvidia
item.description: Cerebras Systems Inc. introduced a new speedier computer built with the company’s chips, saying the device will give it a wider advantage over Nvidia Corp. equipment.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Unitree Robotics Surges 629% After $904 Million Shanghai IPO
item.description: Unitree Robotics shares opened 629% higher in their Shanghai trading debut after raising 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) in an initial public offering that will make it the first publicly traded humanoid robot maker in mainland China.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: AI Boom and Energy Shocks See Growth in Southeast Asia Bifurcate
item.description: Vietnam retained its crown as Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing major economy in the second quarter, with Thailand the laggard, as tech and energy dictated varied fortunes across the region.
item.dc:creator: Srinidhi Ragavendran

item.title: Chip Stocks Slide as Global Bond Anxiety Builds | The Close 8/18/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DoubleLine Capital Deputy CIO Jeffrey Sherman, Higgsfield Co-Founder & CEO Alex Mashrabov, Oppenheimer Managing Director & Senior Analyst Brian Nagel, The Katzen Team Founder Frances Katzen, AlphaSimplex Group Chief Research Strategist Katy Kaminski, Robinhood Chief Brokerage Officer Steve Quirk, Midi Health CEO & Co-Founder Joanna Strober, Fort Robotics CEO Samuel Reeves, & Jefferies Senior Vice President, Equity Research Corey Tarlowe. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CEO of Cuban-Backed Fort Robotics on $500M SPAC Deal
item.description: Fort Robotics, a Philadelphia-based robotics startup backed by Mark Cuban, is planning to go public through a SPAC deal valued at $500 million, with an expected Nasdaq listing under the ticker FROB. Samuel Reeves, CEO of Fort Robotics, explained that the decision to pursue a SPAC rather than a traditional IPO was driven by the need for speed and efficiency to scale the company's technology, operations, go-to-market strategy, and international expansion. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Australia’s Stock Market Seen as AI Haven
item.description: Australia's stock market maybe emerging as a rare safe haven from the AI-driven volatility rattling Asian equities. A nascent rally has pushed valuations to the brink of overtaking India as the Asia-Pacific's priciest major market for the first time in six years. Shaw and Partners Asset Management's Investment Director Julia Lee joins "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" to discuss what this means for index heavyweights like BHP and CSL. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Leaning Into AI Helps VC Founders, Says Revolution's Hall
item.description: David Hall, managing partner at Revolution, talks about how artificial intelligence is helping entrepreneurs of color compete. He speaks with Romaine Bostick at the Bloomberg New Voices event in Martha's Vineyard. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Unitree CEO’s Wealth Jumps $18 Billion After Blockbuster IPO
item.description: Wang Xingxing, the 36-year-old founder of Unitree Robotics, saw his fortune jump by nearly $18 billion after investors looked past new US curbs on the company’s robots to send its shares soaring more than 600% on their first day of trading.
item.dc:creator: Diana Li and Pui Gwen Yeung

item.title: Pony AI Drops as CEO Warns of Uncertainty for Robotaxis
item.description: Pony AI Inc.’s shares dropped for a third day as the loss-making robotaxi firm warned of uncertainties ahead, particularly navigating regulatory hurdles.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Yeo
